hustles.name: Campus errands
hustles.description: Run small errands for busy students. No equipment needed: a good first hustle.

jobs.brief: Chidi needs lecture notes photocopied and delivered before his class. Plan it right.

content.instructions: Order the errand from first to last.

items.text: Confirm the pages, number of copies and deadline with Chidi
Collect the notes and the money for copies
Make the copies at the business centre and keep the receipt
Deliver the copies and the original before his class
Hand over the change and the receipt

jobs.brief: Ada asks you to keep her place in a long queue at the bursary while she is in a test.

content.intro: You're holding a place in a long queue for a classmate.

steps.situation: Someone offers you money to swap your place with theirs.

choices.text: Politely refuse — you're holding it for Ada
choices.feedback: Trustworthy. That's why people hire you again.

choices.text: Accept and tell Ada the queue moved
choices.feedback: Dishonest, and you'd lose the client.

steps.situation: The queue closes early for lunch.

choices.text: Message Ada straight away and ask what she'd like you to do

choices.feedback: Ada will come back to no place and no news.

hustles.name: Campus delivery
hustles.description: Pick up a package at one campus place and deliver it to another — walk it in the 3D world.

jobs.brief: A package is waiting. Pick it up, then deliver it.

hustles.name: Peer tutoring
hustles.description: Help other students with first-year maths and English.

jobs.brief: Bisi is stuck on basic algebra and percentages. Check you can explain them.
Musa wants help with grammar for his first essay.

options.text: Each of the students has a textbook.
Each of the students have a textbook.

questions.prompt: Which word is an adverb? 'She spoke quietly in the library.'
Choose the correct form: 'Their / There / They're going to the lecture.'

hustles.name: Snack sales
hustles.description: Sell snacks near the hostels. Each round uses one batch of snack stock — buy it first.

jobs.brief: Evening rush near the halls. Make good selling decisions.

content.intro: You've set up your cooler box near the hostels at 7 p.m.

choices.text: Near the hall entrance where students walk back from lectures
choices.feedback: Foot traffic is everything in food sales.

choices.text: Behind the building where it's quiet

steps.situation: A customer has only a big note and you have no change.

choices.text: Offer a bank transfer option, or ask a nearby seller to break the note
choices.feedback: Solving payment problems saves the sale.
A lost sale — keep some change next time.

steps.situation: At 9 p.m. you have a few snacks left.

choices.text: Keep them for tomorrow without a cooler
choices.feedback: Food safety first — they may spoil.

hustles.name: Graphic design
hustles.description: Design flyers and logos for campus groups and events.

jobs.brief: The drama society needs a flyer for their show. Get the design basics right.

questions.prompt: The flyer text must be easy to read from far away. What helps most?

options.text: Strong contrast between text and background

questions.prompt: Which file format keeps a logo sharp at any size?
What should be the most prominent thing on the flyer?

options.text: The show's name, date and venue

jobs.brief: Explain design principles to your client by matching them to examples.

content.instructions: Match each principle with an example.

pairs.right: The headline is bigger than the details
Text blocks line up on the same edge
Empty margins that let the design breathe
The same colours and fonts on every page

hustles.name: Photography
hustles.description: Shoot portraits, events and matriculation photos.

jobs.brief: It's matriculation day. Take portraits families will love.

content.intro: Matriculation day: proud families everywhere and a strong afternoon sun.

steps.situation: Harsh midday sun is making faces squint and cast dark shadows.

choices.text: Move subjects into open shade and shoot there
Face them straight into the sun

steps.situation: How do you frame the student in their gown with the faculty building behind?

choices.text: Use the rule of thirds and keep the building visible but not dominant
Cut off their head to fit the whole building

steps.situation: A family asks when they'll get their photos.

choices.text: Agree a clear delivery date and how they'll receive the photos

choices.feedback: Vague promises lead to unhappy clients.

hustles.name: Barbing and grooming
hustles.description: Run a hostel barbing service: neat cuts, clean tools, happy clients.

jobs.brief: Tunde wants a clean low cut before his presentation.

content.instructions: Order the haircut service from start to finish.

items.text: Clean and disinfect the clippers and comb
Ask how short he wants it and check the scalp
Put on a clean cape and neck strip
Cut with the right guard, working evenly
Brush off, show him the mirror and clean up
